rubrics.evidence: The agent patch replaces every inline wireStats field update in the packet sources with a call into MQTTWireStats.c: MQTTSerialize_connect now calls MQTTWireStats_beginSession() and MQTTWireStats_note(1, CONNECT, ...); MQTTDeserialize_connack calls MQTTWireStats_note(0, CONNACK, ...); MQTTSerialize_zero, MQTTSerialize_publish, MQTTDeserialize_publish, MQTTDeserialize_ack, MQTTSerialize_subscribe, MQTTDeserialize_suback, MQTTDeserialize_subscribe, MQTTSerialize_suback, MQTTSerialize_unsubscribe, MQTTDeserialize_unsubscribe, and MQTTSerialize_unsuback all use MQTTWireStats_note plus MQTTWireStats_notePayload/MQTTWireStats_noteTopics as needed; frame counting uses MQTTWireStats_noteFrame; reject paths use MQTTWireStats_noteReject; lastInspected updates use MQTTWireStats_noteInspected. The only remaining direct wireStats field writes in the patch are inside MQTTWireStats.c itself, so no packet-layer function maintains the record inline.
rubrics.criterion: Every update of the wire-activity accounting record in the packet sources is now expressed as a call into the module that owns the record (the statistics helper pair), so no packet-layer function maintains the record's fields inline anymore.

rubrics.evidence: Problem requires identical report values. Patch replaces direct wireStats writes with MQTTWireStats.c functions that perform the same updates: MQTTWireStats_note() bumps per-type sent/received counts and adds the same wirelen to bytesOut/bytesIn; MQTTWireStats_notePayload() adds payload bytes and updates highWaterPayload; MQTTWireStats_beginSession() zeroes session-scoped fields (counts, bytes, payload, highWater, framesIn, decodedTopics) and increments sessionStarts while leaving rejects untouched; MQTTWireStats_noteFrame() is called from both MQTTPacket_read and readnb; MQTTWireStats_noteTopics() adds decodedTopics; MQTTWireStats_noteInspected() sets lastInspected; MQTTWireStats_noteReject() increments rejects. All call sites pass the same lengths/counts as the original direct writes.
rubrics.criterion: The delegated accounting preserves what the report shows today: for identical packet traffic the record still reflects the same per-type send/receive counts, wire byte totals, payload byte totals with the same high-water behavior, session starts plus the session-scoped reset on connect (without clearing lifetime reject totals), rejected packets, accepted frames from both read paths, decoded topic-entry counts, and the last-inspected packet type.

rubrics.evidence: MQTTWireStats.h widens the owning module's API beyond the original MQTTWireStats_note(direction, packettype, wirelen) by declaring MQTTWireStats_notePayload(int outbound, int payloadlen), MQTTWireStats_noteTopics(int count), MQTTWireStats_noteFrame(void), MQTTWireStats_noteReject(void), MQTTWireStats_noteInspected(unsigned char packettype), and MQTTWireStats_beginSession(void). MQTTWireStats.c implements these, and packet code routes facts through them: e.g., MQTTDeserialize_publish calls notePayload, suback/subscribe/unsubscribe call noteTopics, MQTTPacket_read/readnb call noteFrame, truncated ack/unsubscribe paths call noteReject, MQTTFormat calls noteInspected, and MQTTSerialize_connect calls beginSession.
rubrics.criterion: The owning module's public API carries the facts the packet flows produce: entry points and parameters exist for facts the original narrow entry point (direction, packet type, wire length) could not express, such as payload length, list multiplicity, rejection, framing, session lifecycle, and inspected type.

rubrics.evidence: Every listed function's inline record maintenance was replaced with calls into MQTTWireStats.c. MQTTSerialize_connect now calls MQTTWireStats_beginSession() and MQTTWireStats_note(1, CONNECT, ...) instead of the inline loop clearing wireStats fields and direct sentCount/bytesOut writes. MQTTDeserialize_connack, MQTTSerialize_zero, MQTTDeserialize_connect, MQTTSerialize_publish, MQTTDeserialize_publish, MQTTSerialize_subscribe, MQTTDeserialize_suback, MQTTDeserialize_subscribe, MQTTSerialize_suback, MQTTSerialize_unsubscribe, MQTTDeserialize_unsubscribe, and MQTTSerialize_unsuback all replace direct wireStats.sentCount/receivedCount/bytesOut/bytesIn/decodedTopics writes with MQTTWireStats_note(...) and MQTTWireStats_noteTopics(...). The reject branches in MQTTDeserialize_ack and MQTTDeserialize_unsubscribe use MQTTWireStats_noteReject() instead of wireStats.rejects++. MQTTPacket_read and MQTTPacket_readnb use MQTTWireStats_noteFrame() instead of wireStats.framesIn++. MQTTFormat_toClientString and MQTTFormat_toServerString use MQTTWireStats_noteInspected(...) instead of wireStats.lastInspected=. No remaining direct wireStats field writes appear in any of the enumerated functions.
rubrics.criterion: None of the functions that carried inline record maintenance still updates the record directly (including write, increment, or handing the record elsewhere). The hidden locations to verify are: MQTTSerialize_connect, MQTTDeserialize_connack, MQTTSerialize_zero (MQTTConnectClient.c); MQTTDeserialize_connect (MQTTConnectServer.c); MQTTSerialize_publish and MQTTDeserialize_ack's reject branch (MQTTSerializePublish.c, MQTTDeserializePublish.c); MQTTDeserialize_publish (MQTTDeserializePublish.c); MQTTSerialize_subscribe and MQTTDeserialize_suback (MQTTSubscribeClient.c); MQTTDeserialize_subscribe and MQTTSerialize_suback (MQTTSubscribeServer.c); MQTTSerialize_unsubscribe (MQTTUnsubscribeClient.c); MQTTDeserialize_unsubscribe and MQTTSerialize_unsuback (MQTTUnsubscribeServer.c); MQTTPacket_read and MQTTPacket_readnb (MQTTPacket.c); MQTTFormat_toClientString and MQTTFormat_toServerString (MQTTFormat.c).

rubrics.evidence: The patch replaces each inline wireStats mutation with a corresponding MQTTWireStats_* call instead of deleting it: MQTTSerialize_connect calls MQTTWireStats_beginSession() and MQTTWireStats_note(1, CONNECT, ...); MQTTDeserialize_publish calls MQTTWireStats_note(0, PUBLISH, ...) plus MQTTWireStats_notePayload(0, *payloadlen); MQTTPacket_read/readnb call MQTTWireStats_noteFrame(); reject paths call MQTTWireStats_noteReject(); format paths call MQTTWireStats_noteInspected(...). MQTTWireStats.c implements these functions and mutates the same wireStats fields (sentCount/receivedCount, bytesOut/bytesIn, payloadBytes, framesIn, rejects, sessionStarts, decodedTopics, lastInspected), so previously maintained flows are still maintained.
rubrics.criterion: The change does not fix the spread by discarding the accounting: the record is not left unmaintained for flows that maintained it before (for example, simply deleting the inline statements and leaving the record reading zero, or gutting the module so nothing flows into it).

rubrics.evidence: All flow families from the smell.diff are preserved in the agent patch through the new MQTTWireStats entry points: connect lifecycle (MQTTSerialize_connect calls MQTTWireStats_beginSession for session reset + sessionStarts, MQTTDeserialize_connack calls MQTTWireStats_note(0,CONNACK,...), MQTTSerialize_zero calls MQTTWireStats_note(1,packettype,...)); publish both directions with payload+high-water (MQTTSerialize_publish and MQTTDeserialize_publish call MQTTWireStats_note + MQTTWireStats_notePayload); subscribe/unsubscribe and confirmations on client and server sides (MQTTSerialize_subscribe, MQTTDeserialize_suback, MQTTDeserialize_subscribe, MQTTSerialize_suback, MQTTSerialize_unsubscribe, MQTTDeserialize_unsubscribe, MQTTSerialize_unsuback all call MQTTWireStats_note, with MQTTWireStats_noteTopics for decoded topic counts); inbound server-side connect (MQTTDeserialize_connect calls MQTTWireStats_note(0,CONNECT,...)); rejected packets on truncated-input paths (MQTTDeserialize_ack and MQTTDeserialize_unsubscribe call MQTTWireStats_noteReject()); accepted frames from both blocking and non-blocking read paths (MQTTPacket_read and MQTTPacket_readnb both call MQTTWireStats_noteFrame()); both operator formatting views (MQTTFormat_toClientString and MQTTFormat_toServerString call MQTTWireStats_noteInspected). The shared ack serializer's existing MQTTWireStats_note call is left intact. CMakeLists.txt and build_test both add MQTTWireStats.c to builds.
rubrics.criterion: Every flow family that fed the record before the change still feeds it after: the connect lifecycle (session reset and session starts, connack, the shared zero-length/keep-alive path), publish in both directions with payload volume and high-water, subscribe/unsubscribe and their confirmations on both client and server sides, inbound server-side connect, rejected packets on truncated-input paths, accepted frames from both the blocking and the non-blocking read paths, and both operator formatting views.

rubrics.evidence: All record mutations are centralized in MQTTWireStats.c via entry points MQTTWireStats_note, MQTTWireStats_notePayload, MQTTWireStats_noteTopics, MQTTWireStats_noteFrame, MQTTWireStats_noteReject, MQTTWireStats_noteInspected, and MQTTWireStats_beginSession. Consumer files now call these helpers instead of directly writing wireStats fields; e.g., MQTTConnectClient.c uses MQTTWireStats_beginSession() and MQTTWireStats_note(...), MQTTDeserializePublish.c uses MQTTWireStats_note(...) and MQTTWireStats_notePayload(...), MQTTPacket.c uses MQTTWireStats_noteFrame(), and MQTTFormat.c uses MQTTWireStats_noteInspected(...). No bookkeeping helper that updates the record was introduced inside individual consumer files.
rubrics.criterion: Ownership stays coherent after the change: the record and all its update entry points live in the single statistics module source pair, and no bookkeeping helper that updates the record was introduced separately inside individual consumer files (which would re-create the scattered policy in a new shape).

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch maintains a single shared record `MQTTWireStats wireStats = {0};` in MQTTWireStats.c and routes all mutations through functions in that module (MQTTWireStats_note, MQTTWireStats_notePayload, MQTTWireStats_noteTopics, MQTTWireStats_noteFrame, MQTTWireStats_noteReject, MQTTWireStats_noteInspected, MQTTWireStats_beginSession). All per-file direct field accesses from the smell (e.g., `wireStats.sentCount[CONNECT]++`, `wireStats.bytesOut += ...`, `wireStats.framesIn++`) are replaced with calls to these functions, and no second record, parallel counter set, or per-module copy of any accounting field is introduced.
rubrics.criterion: The change does not introduce a second shared record, a parallel counter set, or per-module copies of any accounting field that would have to be kept in sync alongside the original record.

rubrics.evidence: The patch removes the scratch declaration `int i = 0;` from MQTTSerialize_connect and replaces the inline session-reset/counter block with `MQTTWireStats_beginSession();` and `MQTTWireStats_note(1, CONNECT, ...)`. In all other affected files, direct `wireStats` field writes are replaced by `MQTTWireStats_*` calls, and each retained `#include "MQTTWireStats.h"` is still used for those function prototypes. No leftover loop index, dead branch, or unused owning-module include remains in the consumer functions.
rubrics.criterion: No debris of the inline maintenance remains in the affected functions: scratch declarations that existed only to support it (for example, a loop index declared solely to clear the counters), leftover comment lines describing the old inline bookkeeping, dead branches left by removing it, and no consumer file keeps a mention of the owning module that it no longer references.

rubrics.evidence: MQTTWireStats.h declares seven public functions, and every one has at least one call site in the packet sources: MQTTWireStats_note is called in MQTTConnectClient.c, MQTTConnectServer.c, MQTTDeserializePublish.c, MQTTSerializePublish.c (both MQTTSerialize_publish and the fixed-length ack serializer MQTTSerialize_ack retained from the smell diff), MQTTSubscribeClient.c, MQTTSubscribeServer.c, MQTTUnsubscribeClient.c, and MQTTUnsubscribeServer.c; MQTTWireStats_notePayload in MQTTDeserializePublish.c and MQTTSerializePublish.c; MQTTWireStats_noteTopics in MQTTSubscribeClient.c, MQTTSubscribeServer.c, and MQTTUnsubscribeServer.c; MQTTWireStats_noteFrame in MQTTPacket.c (both MQTTPacket_read and MQTTPacket_readnb); MQTTWireStats_noteReject in MQTTDeserializePublish.c and MQTTUnsubscribeServer.c; MQTTWireStats_noteInspected in MQTTFormat.c (both toClientString and toServerString); MQTTWireStats_beginSession in MQTTConnectClient.c. No declared public entry point lacks a caller.
rubrics.criterion: The statistics module exposes no dead public surface after the change: every public entry point it declares has at least one calling site in the packet sources (the original narrow entry point is fine to keep if the conforming fixed-length ack serializer still calls it).

rubrics.evidence: Every packet-function hunk only replaces direct wireStats field updates with MQTTWireStats_* calls; no hunk adds/removes serialization writes (writeChar, writeInt, writeMQTTString, MQTTPacket_encode, memcpy) or alters rc=/return statements. E.g., MQTTSerialize_connect still ends with rc = ptr - buf; after MQTTWireStats_note(1, CONNECT, ...); MQTTDeserialize_ack still does MQTTWireStats_noteReject(); goto exit; on truncation and rc = 1; on success; MQTTPacket_read/readnb still set rc = header.bits.type after MQTTWireStats_noteFrame(). No serializer, deserializer, or read-path function signature is modified.
rubrics.criterion: The packet layer's externally observable behavior is unchanged: serialized byte layouts, public function signatures, and return codes of every serializer, deserializer, and read path are the same as before the change.

rubrics.evidence: The patch routes each update through the same event-specific helper at the same site: rejected acks/unsubscribes call MQTTWireStats_noteReject() and goto exit before any MQTTWireStats_note(0,...), so rejects are not tallied as received; MQTTWireStats_beginSession() zeroes only session-scoped fields and then increments sessionStarts, leaving rejects untouched; MQTTWireStats_noteFrame() remains at the readnb rem_len==0 completion transition; and both MQTTFormat_toClientString and MQTTFormat_toServerString call MQTTWireStats_noteInspected(). No call site adds a second note for the same packet/bytes.
rubrics.criterion: No accounting value moved to a different event than the one it describes: a packet is not counted twice for the same wire traffic (for example by accounting at both a caller and a callee), rejected packets are not tallied as received, the session reset does not clear lifetime counters (reject totals, session starts), the non-blocking completion is not counted at the wrong state-machine transition, and the inspected-type viewport is not captured for only one of the two formatting views.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch adds no malloc/calloc/realloc and no new static buffers beyond the existing `wireStats` record. Per-packet accounting functions (`MQTTWireStats_note`, `notePayload`, `noteTopics`, `noteFrame`, `noteReject`, `noteInspected`) perform only O(1) increments/additions/assignments. `MQTTWireStats_beginSession` loops over fixed `MQTTWIRESTATS_TYPE_COUNT` (15) at session start, independent of packet or list sizes, and is not a per-packet hot path.
rubrics.criterion: The packet layer remains suitable for small embedded targets: the delegation introduces no dynamic allocation and no new static buffers, and the per-packet bookkeeping stays constant-time relative to packet and list sizes (no new scanning of the record or buffers on hot paths).
